risks: Engine distress vetoes E1/E2/E4 are demerger-accounting artifacts: FY26 PAT Rs 5,361 cr includes ~Rs 5,325 cr non-cash realty-demerger gain; FY25 PAT Rs 7,636 cr includes ~Rs 7,366 cr lifestyle-demerger gain — Sloan ratio 1.12 trips the screen mechanically
Operating economics are thin: FY26 PBT pre-exceptional Rs 99 cr on Rs 2,212 cr sales (4.5% margin); operating PAT ~Rs 54 cr; operating ROE ~1.9% on Rs 2,844 cr book
Valuation stretched on operating numbers: ~152x FY26 operating EPS (Rs 8.04), 2.9x book, EV/EBITDA 23.7x; stock +282% from 52-week low Rs 320 — the aerospace re-rating prices flawless execution
Concentration: aerospace & defence draws 58% of revenue from Europe, 20% from the US; exports >50% of total business — tariff/geopolitical sensitivity
Execution risk on Rs 930 cr Gudipalli capex and aerospace program scale-up; Aero EBITDA margin compressed to 21.2% (from 23.7%) on R&D investments
Dilution overhang: 33.3L Minerva warrants @ Rs 645 (~4.35% fully diluted); promoter pledge spiked to 15.25% in Mar-2026 before full release by Jun-2026
Only FY25/FY26 are post-demerger comparable — FY24 and earlier include lifestyle + realty, so all multi-year vendor trends (e.g. -8.5% sales CAGR, 131% 3-yr ROE) are meaningless
thesis: Post two demergers, NSE:RAYMOND is a pure-play engineering company (precision technology & auto components + aerospace & defence) — not the textiles/realty conglomerate its price history suggests. The engine excludes it on earnings-quality vetoes, but all three trips are mechanical artifacts of ~Rs 12,700 cr of non-cash demerger gains flowing through FY25/FY26 P&L, not operating fraud. The real question is valuation: the operating business earns ~Rs 54 cr PAT against an Rs 8,100 cr market cap (~152x operating earnings) while the market prices a flawless ten-year aerospace scale-up. PASS — the re-rating has run ahead of the earnings.
